title: Typed operator languages
summary: Extend single-space exact observability to finite typed action graphs with rectangular maps, legal-path witnesses, per-type minimal linear quotients and independently replayed graph adapters.
acceptance: Finite declared type grammar genuinely closes at fixed budget.
Certify L_b=A_b B_b and B_target M_a=T_a B_source with actual legal experiment witnesses.
Compare all short legal graph paths against direct assembled-graph height enumeration.
Verify cheapest exact witnesses separately from robust margin optimization.

pushes.title: Typed algebra contract
pushes.acceptance: Prove typed closure, quotient invariance and linear minimality; test exact rectangular fixture, empty outputs, malformed dimensions and illegal paths.

pushes.title: Graph adapters
pushes.acceptance: Compile a finite boundary grammar and independently enumerate actual graphs for every retained short legal path, including noncommuting order and duplicate-edge rejection.

pushes.title: Certificates and costs
pushes.acceptance: Replay portable identities without compiler invocation and compare cheapest witnesses with bounded exhaustive legal-path search, including rank-zero types and chronology tampering.

title: Parameter-wide observable modules
summary: Extend existing Q[q] observation modules beyond current budgets, with exact rank strata, denominator guards, module-generation certificates and resource-aware exceptional-parameter classification.
acceptance: Preserve distinction between generic rank and complete polynomial observation module.
Reproduce false and true q=1/2 exceptional examples independently.
Attempt next budget under explicit degree, bit, step and time limits; incomplete factorization is explicit.
Provide exact roots/ranks and bases on certified parameter regions; sampling alone is insufficient.

pushes.title: Resource-bounded module certificates
pushes.acceptance: Implement strict receipt states, replay module/divisor identities and tamper tests; compare tiny explicit-word minors with independent polynomial arithmetic.

pushes.title: Next graph budgets
pushes.acceptance: Attempt R=5 first with logged resource bounds; compare rational specializations with exact closure and report any refusal without a false interval theorem.

pushes.title: Parameter atlas and explanation
pushes.acceptance: Produce certified parameter-cell bases and exceptional ranks, plus a bounded rational-function example with explicit pole guards and independent specialization checks.

title: Graph-realizable invisible directions
summary: Search actual two-terminal graph pairs constrained by degree, slice and charge compatibility, distinguishing formal null vectors from realizations and bounded exclusions from full-series theorems.
acceptance: Retain rational-parameter interpolation and exact context-language hypotheses.
Reproduce R=38 and R=11 as candidate frontiers only.
Verify filters never discard a valid tiny pair, and preserve labeled height multiplicities.
Return a fully checked graph pair or a complete explicitly bounded exclusion with population completeness evidence.

pushes.title: Realization specification and filters
pushes.acceptance: Reproduce frontier vectors and slice restrictions; validate degree/charge filters against direct tiny graph kernels.

pushes.title: Complete bounded families
pushes.acceptance: Exhaust at least two declared bounded structural families, independently check constructor completeness and surviving kernels, and record every bound and resource limit.

pushes.title: Witness or rigidity advance
pushes.acceptance: Exhibit an actual full truncated-kernel witness and glued-observation checks, or prove a new stated structural exclusion; never turn finite agreement into full-series equality.

title: Incremental connected-support compilation
summary: Compile exact local changes to nonnegative integral weighted graph energies using union-graph supports, ambient-degree-aware cache invalidation and independent full-recompilation checks.
acceptance: Use the union of old/new support graphs for insertion/deletion completeness.
Invalidate every support touching changed endpoints, including singleton ambient-degree changes.
Verify weighted nonnegative energy and ordinary integral q exponents with zero edges represented as absence.
Compare sequential/reversed edits to independent composition enumeration and report setup-inclusive bit/runtime costs.

pushes.title: Weighted locality contract
pushes.acceptance: Prove the union-support difference identity, implement nonnegative integral weight changes and reproduce the exact two-vertex coefficient/log example.

pushes.title: Incremental cache and updates
pushes.acceptance: Check all small edge edits, sequential edits, reversal, pinning changes, stale patches and cross-graph cache isolation against full recompilation and direct energy enumeration.

pushes.title: Scaling and reusable receipts
pushes.acceptance: Demonstrate exact bounded-degree local reuse at fixed budget; report updated supports, polynomial operations, coefficient bits, setup cost and replay time separately.

title: Low-rank physical fault transport
summary: Reuse a nominal discrete thermal resolvent across rank-one bond removals and small multi-fault corrections, preserving fault identity, source provenance, finite-horizon exactness and uncertainty contracts.
acceptance: Use A_fault=A_nominal+delta*b*b^T for removed nonnegative conductance.
Check rank-one and Woodbury formulas against independent neighbor-flux updates and direct sparse powers.
Preserve row sums, candidate identities, source-derived units and finite-horizon uncertainty boundaries.
Benchmark all 264 plate bonds with setup, coefficient-bit and memory costs, without presupposing speedup.

pushes.title: Exact rank-one contract
pushes.acceptance: Reproduce two-node transfer cancellation, partial/zero blockage, bond reversal and source sign/row-sum checks using independent flux and power oracles.

pushes.title: Multi-fault and protocol reuse
pushes.acceptance: Check every pair in a small catalogue at multiple severities, arbitrary short input words and nonzero initial states; reject impossible removal severities.

pushes.title: Full plate population benchmark
pushes.acceptance: Cover all 264 bonds at a declared horizon, independently verify selected outputs and reflected blindness, and report setup-inclusive break-even count, bits and runtime.

title: Recovery conditioning and bit complexity
summary: Quantify exact inverse noise amplification, target-specific recovery, finite-difference cancellation and encoded bit growth across delayed, weighted and charge-based interface recovery.
acceptance: Verify exact left-inverse identities and componentwise box-noise bounds.
Separate physical noise from rescaling/postprocessing noise and exact-rank pruning from robust optimization.
Compare probe count, volume, cost, amplification and encoded bits on equal declared targets.
Certify one target-error design optimum and any parameter-wide bounds, without inferring interval results from samples.

pushes.title: Exact amplification contract
pushes.acceptance: Prove and implement inverse error bounds, attain 32epsilon/33epsilon tiny-example bounds by box vertices, and retain dependent-row robust and rescaling counterexamples.

pushes.title: Recovery family comparison
pushes.acceptance: Compare finite differences, weighted restoration and charge charts against direct tiny graph kernels with complete volume/cost/noise/bit accounting.

pushes.title: Certified target design
pushes.acceptance: Certify the least-cost design from a bounded menu satisfying target error; replay rational primal/dual witnesses and compact-interval bounds independently.
